blurb: Practice questions reused from openly licensed sources for the Marketing exam. Most of this exam is still a placeholder: see the note below.
disclaimer: Questions reused from openly licensed sources (credited on each question). Not official DECA exam content.
placeholderNote: Only 1 openly licensed item is cleared for the Marketing exam right now. Almost every source that SOURCES.md maps to this exam is an OpenStax book, and OpenStax forbids ingestion into large language models or generative AI without its written permission, so the 94 OpenStax items built for this exam are held in _hold-openstax/exams/marketing.json until the owner gets that permission. The only other mapped source, Business Writing For Everyone (KPU, CC BY-NC 4.0), has 45 H5P activities but just one four-option, single-answer multiple-choice item (SOURCES.md estimated 2; a scan of all 45 found 1). Of its other 18 multiple-choice items, 11 are single-answer with 3 options (usable only if the owner allows 3-choice items, SOURCES.md 7.2) and 7 have just 2 options (not usable). None were padded to 4 choices. Every area without items is a labelled placeholder (see placeholders).
licenceNote: Business Writing For Everyone is "licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 International License, except where otherwise noted" (book home page and the Reviewing CMAPP page, checked 2026-10-11). NonCommercial: DECA Masters must stay free and non-commercial to use it. Show each item's attribution line wherever the item appears; credit Kwantlen Polytechnic University by name only, no logo, no implied endorsement.
areaNote: Areas follow the DECA 2026-27 Marketing exam blueprint, association-level counts (SOURCES.md 3 and 5.6). targetCount is that count; haveCount is what this file holds; heldOpenStaxCount is what waits in _hold-openstax.
difficultyNote: Difficulty is an estimate by the building agent after reading the item (1 = recall, the answer is one of the question list given in the section). Not rated by a person.

questions.stem: When choosing a genre, which of the following questions should you ask yourself?
choices: How quickly does my audience need this information?
How does my audience expect to receive this information?
What way is this information normally sent in my organization?
questions.explanation: From "Reviewing CMAPP" (Chapter 6: Writing Emails, Memos, Letters and Instant Messages): "Here are some questions you can ask yourself before you choose a genre: How quickly does my audience need this information? How does my audience expect to receive this information? How will my audience use this information? ... What way is this information normally sent in my organization?" Each of the first three choices is on that list, so the keyed answer is "All of the above."
